title: Monte Carlo Methods
description: When a sum is too hard to do, guess it at random - many times. The scatter of the guesses falls as one over the square root of how many; steer them well and it falls faster. Unlocks the Monte Carlo Engine.

puzzle.goal: A Markov chain gives N samples of a quantity with spread σ, but each sample remembers the last: they stay correlated for about τ steps. Averaged, they are worth fewer independent samples. Write how far their average typically is from the truth, ε.
puzzle.name: Standard error of a correlated chain
puzzle.ask: Find ε for a chain of spread s = @{s}, correlation time t = @{t} steps, and N = @{N} samples.
puzzle.method: Independent samples average to σ/√N. Correlated ones are worth only N/(1 + 2τ) independent ones - the effective sample size.
